# National Grid Prepares for Winter, Connects Massachusetts Customers with Energy Assistance


- [Home](https://www.nationalgrid.com/)
- [News](https://www.nationalgrid.com/news)


24th November 2026


*News*


#### *Customer webinar set for Monday, November 30, with in-person assistance events planned across Massachusetts in December*


**WALTHAM, MA** – With winter approaching and a storm expected to affect parts of Massachusetts later this week, National Grid has prepared its electric and gas systems to serve customers through storms and periods of high energy demand, while also connecting customers with programs and resources that can help manage winter energy costs.


On Monday, November 30,[National Grid will host a virtual customer webinar](https://webinars.questline.com/questline-inc/national-grid-presents-fall-customer-bill-assistance-webinar-6404fde50b0b) to provide information about available bill assistance, payment options, and other resources. Customers can hear directly from National Grid representatives about the support available to them and how to access it.


Throughout December, National Grid will also host in-person customer assistance events across Massachusetts, giving customers an opportunity to meet one-on-one with customer advocates to discuss their individual circumstances and determine what programs and resources may be available to them.


“We prepare for winter all year long, investing in our electric and gas systems, planning for periods of high demand, and making sure our customers have access to the support they need,” said Lisa Wieland, President of National Grid New England. “New England faces real energy supply constraints, particularly during the coldest days of the year, which is why we need to make the most of all the resources available to us while continuing to invest in the systems our customers rely on every day. Above all, we want our customers to know that we are prepared for winter, and we are here to help.”


Across New England, National Grid’s winter preparations include investments and operational planning designed to strengthen its electric and gas systems and maintain safe, reliable service for customers. Preparations include:


**Storm readiness** : National Grid prepares year-round for severe weather, investing in technologies like[Fault, Location, Isolation and Service Restoration (FLISR) that help restore electric service faster](https://www.nationalgrid.com/about-us/innovation/flisr) ,[vegetation management](https://www.nationalgrid.com/us/ma/electric/home/safety-outages/electrical-safety/trees-and-your-electric-service/vegetation-management-program) , worker training, and emergency response procedures that allow teams to respond across the territory. FLISR now serves more than 35 percent of National Grid’s Massachusetts electric customers and has restored service in under a minute during major weather events.


As storms approach,[National Grid closely monitors forecasts and begins coordinating staffing, equipment, materials, and response centers based on expected impacts](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/ApG3fKwYmXk) . The company can also mobilize additional contractors and mutual-assistance crews when widespread damage is expected, positioning crews and equipment in advance so restoration can begin as quickly and safely as conditions allow.


**Natural gas readiness** : Natural gas plays a[critical role in meeting New England’s energy needs](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NSplDS3GvLA) during the winter. In Massachusetts, National Grid maintains more than 11,300 miles of natural gas distribution mains, including an extensive network of older infrastructure that requires ongoing maintenance and investment to ensure safe, reliable service.


Winter cold also places significant demand on New England’s constrained energy supply. Limited natural gas pipeline capacity into the region can restrict access to supply during periods of peak demand, underscoring the need for an all-of-the-above approach that maintains reliable natural gas service alongside other energy resources. To help meet that demand, National Grid maintains a network of liquefied natural gas (LNG) facilities that provide additional gas supply on the[coldest days of the year](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/eWQeUDjfxRU) . National Grid prepares those facilities ahead of the winter heating season, procuring and storing LNG when demand is lower so that additional supply is available when customers need it most.


Last winter, these LNG supplies provided more than 20 percent of the total gas throughput[serving National Grid’s Massachusetts customers](https://www.nationalgridus.com/News/National-Grid-Gas-System-Performs-Reliably-Across-Massachusetts-During-Prolonged-Extreme-Cold/) on the coldest days, helping the natural gas system perform safely and reliably through prolonged periods of extreme cold.


**Customer support** : Gas and electric customers across Massachusetts are supported by National Grid customer advocates and service teams that can connect them with programs and resources to help manage their energy bills during the winter heating season. These include the[tiered discount rate](https://www.nationalgridus.com/MA-Home/Payment-Assistance-Programs/Discount-Rates) , now available to eligible gas customers, as well as programs such as the[Budget Plan,](https://www.nationalgridus.com/MA-Home/Bill-Help/Budget-Plan) which helps customers spread their energy costs more evenly across all 12 months of the year.


Customers can learn more about these and other bill-assistance options during National Grid’s[November 30 webinar](https://webinars.questline.com/questline-inc/national-grid-presents-fall-customer-bill-assistance-webinar-6404fde50b0b) or by meeting one-on-one with customer advocates at[in-person Customer Assistance events](https://www.nationalgridus.com/customer-assistance-events) across Massachusetts throughout December. The events are free and open to the public, and customers are encouraged to visit the Massachusetts Customer Assistance event page to confirm the date, time, and location of each session.

**Additional Customer Resources**


National Grid offers additional programs and resources for customers who need help managing their energy costs, including payment arrangements, income-eligible assistance, and energy-efficiency programs. Customers can visit[National Grid’s website to learn more about available bill assistance and payment options](https://www.nationalgrid.com/us/ma/gas/home/here-for-you) .


Customers can also find information online about[saving energy and reducing heating costs](https://www.nationalgridus.com/MA-Gas-Home/energy-saving-tips/?regionkey=massgas&customertype=home&intendedUrl=%2Fregionalized%2FEnergy-Saving-Tips%2F%3F) , along with[important winter gas and appliance safety guidance](https://www.nationalgridus.com/ma-home/Natural-Gas-Safety/Appliance-Safety.aspx?linkId=219111007) .


## About National Grid


National Grid (NYSE: NGG) delivers electricity and natural gas to more than 20 million people across New York and Massachusetts. We’re committed to meeting our customers’ energy needs and supporting economic growth across the regions we serve—providing safe, reliable energy today and building the resilient networks of the future. National Grid Ventures, our commercial business, develops and operates infrastructure that delivers affordable and reliable energy to consumers. National Grid Partners, our venture capital and corporate innovation arm, invests in and collaborates with technology companies that are accelerating the future of energy and helping new technologies reach critical scale faster.


For more information, please visit our[website](https://www.nationalgrid.com/) , follow us on[X](https://x.com/nationalgridus) , watch us on[YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/user/NationalGrid) , like us on[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/nationalgrid) and find us on[Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/nationalgrid/) .
